name: Classes
definition: An object-oriented programming construct that defines the attributes/state and operations/behaviour shared by objects of the class.
scope: Class definitions, objects/instances, attributes, methods, encapsulation, abstraction, constructors, visibility and implementation of abstract data types.
core_principles: Abstraction; encapsulation; state and behaviour; modularity; information hiding.
semantic_description: Classes provide a blueprint for objects by combining state representation with operations. They support abstraction and encapsulation and are commonly used to implement reusable data abstractions.
keywords_synonyms: Object-oriented programming; data abstraction; ADTs
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Stacks
definition: A linear abstract data type in which insertion and deletion occur at one designated end, following last-in-first-out (LIFO) order.
scope: Push, pop, peek/top, underflow/overflow conditions, array- and linked implementations, and time/space complexity.
core_principles: LIFO ordering; abstraction; access restriction; operation complexity.
semantic_description: A stack restricts access to the most recently inserted element. Its operations are typically O(1) with suitable implementations and it is used for recursion, expression evaluation and backtracking.
keywords_synonyms: LIFO; push/pop; ADT; underflow/overflow
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Queues
definition: A linear abstract data type in which insertion is performed at one end and deletion at the other, following first-in-first-out (FIFO) order.
scope: Enqueue, dequeue, front/rear operations, circular queues, array/linked implementations, and underflow/overflow conditions.
core_principles: FIFO ordering; abstraction; controlled access; operation complexity.
semantic_description: A queue models ordered service in which the earliest inserted item is normally removed first. Circular and linked implementations can provide efficient enqueue/dequeue operations.
keywords_synonyms: FIFO; enqueue/dequeue; circular queue; ADT
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Linked Lists
definition: A linked linear data structure consisting of nodes that contain data and one or more links to other nodes.
scope: Singly, doubly and circular lists; insertion/deletion; traversal; node references; memory representation and complexity.
core_principles: Dynamic linkage; pointer/reference integrity; structural flexibility; operation complexity.
semantic_description: Linked lists represent sequences through node links rather than contiguous storage. They support efficient insertion/deletion when the relevant position or node is known, but sequential access is required for traversal.
keywords_synonyms: Nodes; pointers/references; dynamic data structures
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Binary Search Tree (BST)
definition: A binary tree in which keys in the left subtree are ordered relative to the node key and keys in the right subtree are ordered in the opposite direction, according to the chosen ordering rule.
scope: Search, insertion, deletion, traversal, ordering invariant, height and best/average/worst-case complexity.
core_principles: Ordering invariant; recursive structure; search efficiency; height dependence.
semantic_description: A binary search tree maintains an ordering property that supports ordered search and update operations. Its performance depends on tree height, ranging from logarithmic for balanced shapes to linear for a degenerate tree.
keywords_synonyms: Binary trees; ordering; recursion
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: AVL Trees
definition: A self-balancing binary search tree in which the height difference between the left and right subtrees of every node is bounded by one.
scope: Balance factor, rotations, insertion/deletion rebalancing, search and height guarantees.
core_principles: Height balance; ordering invariant; rotations; logarithmic height.
semantic_description: AVL trees maintain the BST ordering property while using rotations after updates to keep height logarithmic, giving O(log n) search, insertion and deletion in the standard model.
keywords_synonyms: BST; balance factor; rotations
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Quick/Merge sort
definition: Comparison-based sorting methods represented here by Quicksort and Mergesort, which organize elements into sorted order using divide-and-conquer strategies.
scope: Partitioning and recursive subproblems in Quicksort; splitting and merging in Mergesort; stability, in-place behaviour and time/space complexity.
core_principles: Divide and conquer; ordering; complexity; partitioning/merging.
semantic_description: Quicksort partitions around a pivot and has average O(n log n) time but O(n²) worst-case time for poor pivot choices. Mergesort uses merging of sorted sublists and has O(n log n) time, typically requiring additional storage for arrays.
keywords_synonyms: Quicksort; Mergesort; divide and conquer
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Binary Search
definition: A search algorithm that repeatedly compares a target with the middle element of an ordered sequence and eliminates half of the remaining search interval.
scope: Sorted data requirement, iterative/recursive implementation, interval reduction and complexity.
core_principles: Ordering; divide and conquer; logarithmic search.
semantic_description: Binary search achieves O(log n) comparisons when applied to an ordered structure that supports efficient midpoint access, such as an array.
keywords_synonyms: Sorted sequence; comparison; interval halving
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Collision resolution
definition: Techniques used in hash tables to handle multiple keys that map to the same table location.
scope: Separate chaining, open addressing, probing strategies, load factor and clustering effects.
core_principles: Hashing; occupancy/load factor; collision management; expected constant-time access under suitable assumptions.
semantic_description: Collision resolution preserves correct hash-table operations when distinct keys produce the same hash-table index. Performance depends on the hash function, load factor and resolution strategy.
keywords_synonyms: Hash functions; hash tables; load factor
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Truth tables
definition: A tabular method for evaluating the truth value of a propositional or logical expression for every possible assignment of its component propositions.
scope: Logical connectives, compound propositions, equivalence, tautology, contradiction and satisfiability checks.
core_principles: Boolean semantics; compositional evaluation; logical equivalence.
semantic_description: Truth tables provide exhaustive finite evaluation of propositional expressions and can establish equivalence or identify tautological and contradictory forms.
keywords_synonyms: Propositional logic; Boolean algebra; Boolean semantics; compositional evaluation; logical equivalence; Discrete Mathematics
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Induction
definition: A proof method in which a statement is established for an initial case and then shown to hold for the next case assuming it holds for the current case.
scope: Weak/ordinary induction, strong induction, base case, inductive hypothesis and inductive step.
core_principles: Logical implication; well-founded progression; proof by cases over natural-number structure.
semantic_description: Mathematical induction proves statements over suitably ordered discrete domains by combining a base case with an inductive argument. Strong induction permits use of multiple earlier cases.
keywords_synonyms: Logic; natural numbers; proof techniques
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Equivalence relations
definition: A binary relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, thereby partitioning a set into equivalence classes.
scope: Relation properties, equivalence classes, partitions and representative elements.
core_principles: Reflexivity; symmetry; transitivity; partitioning.
semantic_description: An equivalence relation identifies elements that are considered equivalent under the relation and induces a partition of the underlying set into disjoint equivalence classes.
keywords_synonyms: Relations; sets; partitions
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Pigeonhole principle
definition: A counting principle stating that placing more objects than containers into those containers forces at least one container to contain more than one object.
scope: Basic and generalized forms, counting arguments and existence proofs.
core_principles: Counting; cardinality; unavoidable repetition.
semantic_description: The pigeonhole principle establishes existence results by comparing the cardinalities of objects and available categories without requiring construction of the repeated case.
keywords_synonyms: Sets; counting; cardinality
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Trees
definition: A connected acyclic graph used to represent hierarchical or recursive relationships.
scope: Rooted trees, parent/child relationships, degree, height, depth, traversal and common tree representations.
core_principles: Hierarchy; connectivity; acyclicity; recursive decomposition.
semantic_description: Trees provide hierarchical representations with unique paths between nodes in the underlying undirected tree. Rooted trees support traversal and recursive algorithms.
keywords_synonyms: Graphs; recursion; tree traversal
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Entities, relationships & constraints
definition: Core components of conceptual database modelling in which entities represent distinguishable objects, relationships represent associations, and constraints specify valid states.
scope: Entity sets, attributes, relationship sets, cardinality/participation constraints, keys and integrity constraints.
core_principles: Data modelling; integrity; identity; structural constraints.
semantic_description: Conceptual database modelling captures information requirements independently of physical storage. Entities and relationships are constrained to preserve semantic and integrity requirements.
keywords_synonyms: ER modelling; keys; integrity constraints
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Relational algebra
definition: A formal procedural query language based on operations over relations, producing relations as results.
scope: Selection, projection, union, difference, Cartesian product, joins, renaming and derived operations.
core_principles: Closure; relational composition; set semantics; query transformation.
semantic_description: Relational algebra provides a mathematical basis for relational query processing. Operators transform relations while preserving a relation-valued result.
keywords_synonyms: Relations; selection; projection; joins
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: SQL queries
definition: Declarative statements used to define, retrieve, manipulate and control data in relational database systems.
scope: SELECT queries, filtering, joins, grouping, aggregation, subqueries and data modification statements.
core_principles: Declarative querying; set-oriented processing; integrity; transaction semantics.
semantic_description: SQL expresses database operations at a logical level while the DBMS determines an execution strategy. Query correctness depends on relational semantics, constraints and transaction context.
keywords_synonyms: Relational model; relational algebra; joins
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Boyce-Codd Normal Form
definition: A relational normal form in which every determinant of a non-trivial functional dependency is a superkey.
scope: Functional dependencies, candidate keys, determinants, decomposition and lossless/dependency-preserving considerations.
core_principles: Functional dependency; key-based determination; redundancy reduction.
semantic_description: BCNF strengthens normalization by requiring every non-trivial functional dependency to have a superkey determinant. Decomposition may be needed to remove update anomalies.
keywords_synonyms: Functional dependencies; candidate keys; 3NF
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Concurrency control
definition: Database mechanisms that coordinate concurrent transactions so that their interleaved execution preserves required correctness properties.
scope: Serializability, locking, timestamps, isolation, conflicts, deadlock interaction and recovery considerations.
core_principles: Isolation; serializability; consistency; conflict management.
semantic_description: Concurrency control regulates interleaved transactions to prevent undesirable anomalies while allowing useful parallelism. Common approaches include two-phase locking and timestamp-based methods.
keywords_synonyms: Transactions; serializability; locking
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Deadlocks
definition: A state in which a set of processes or threads are permanently blocked because each waits for a resource or event held or controlled by another member of the set.
scope: Necessary conditions, resource-allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery.
core_principles: Mutual exclusion; hold-and-wait; circular wait; resource allocation.
semantic_description: Operating-system deadlock analysis identifies cyclic waiting dependencies and methods for preventing, avoiding, detecting or recovering from them.
keywords_synonyms: Resource allocation; process synchronization; Mutual exclusion; hold-and-wait; circular wait; Operating Systems
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Thread synchronization
definition: Coordination mechanisms that control the ordering and mutual access of concurrent threads to shared state.
scope: Critical sections, mutexes/locks, semaphores, monitors, condition variables, race conditions and atomicity.
core_principles: Mutual exclusion; ordering; atomicity; visibility.
semantic_description: Thread synchronization prevents or controls race conditions and establishes required ordering between concurrent operations accessing shared resources.
keywords_synonyms: Concurrency; critical sections; locks
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Scheduling algorithms
definition: Algorithms used by an operating system to select processes or threads for execution and allocate processor time.
scope: FCFS, SJF/SRTF, priority, round-robin and multilevel scheduling; response, waiting and turnaround metrics.
core_principles: Fairness; responsiveness; throughput; processor utilization.
semantic_description: CPU scheduling determines execution order under stated policies and objectives. Different algorithms trade off response time, waiting time, throughput and fairness.
keywords_synonyms: Processes/threads; CPU management; Fairness; responsiveness; throughput; processor utilization
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Paging and virtual memory
definition: Memory-management techniques that divide address spaces into pages and physical memory into frames, allowing virtual addresses to be mapped to physical locations.
scope: Page tables, address translation, page faults, demand paging, replacement and working-set considerations.
core_principles: Address-space abstraction; locality; protection; memory utilization.
semantic_description: Paging separates virtual address spaces from physical memory. Virtual memory can extend the apparent address space and support protection, but page faults incur substantial latency.
keywords_synonyms: Memory management; address translation; Address-space abstraction; locality; protection; memory utilization
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: File allocation and organization
definition: Methods by which an operating system organizes files and allocates storage blocks to represent their contents.
scope: Contiguous, linked and indexed allocation, directories, free-space management and access patterns.
core_principles: Storage organization; locality; allocation efficiency; reliability.
semantic_description: File allocation determines how file blocks are placed and accessed on storage. Choices affect sequential/random access, fragmentation, metadata overhead and reliability.
keywords_synonyms: File systems; storage management; Storage organization; locality; allocation efficiency; reliability
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
definition: The arithmetic logic unit is a processor datapath component that performs arithmetic, logical and related bitwise operations on operands.
scope: Arithmetic operations, logical operations, flags/status outputs, operand width and datapath integration.
core_principles: Combinational logic; arithmetic; Boolean operations; datapath design.
semantic_description: The ALU implements fundamental computational operations within a processor datapath. Its design influences instruction execution, latency, area and energy use.
keywords_synonyms: Processor datapath; arithmetic circuits; Combinational logic; arithmetic; Boolean operations; datapath design
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Reduced Instruction Set Computer / Complex Instruction Set Computer (RISC/CISC)
definition: Two broad instruction-set design approaches distinguished by how instruction complexity, encoding, addressing and implementation responsibilities are organized.
scope: Instruction complexity, instruction formats, addressing modes, register use, code density and implementation trade-offs.
core_principles: Instruction-set abstraction; implementation trade-offs; performance; code density.
semantic_description: RISC designs generally favor simpler, more regular instructions, while CISC designs may provide richer instruction semantics. Modern processors can combine characteristics of both approaches.
keywords_synonyms: Instruction sets; processor architecture; Instruction-set abstraction; implementation trade-offs; performance; code density
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Pipeline hazards
definition: Conditions in a pipelined processor that prevent the next instruction from proceeding through the pipeline as scheduled.
scope: Structural, data and control hazards; stalls, forwarding, scheduling and branch handling.
core_principles: Pipeline parallelism; dependency management; throughput.
semantic_description: Pipeline hazards arise from resource conflicts, data dependencies or control-flow changes. Hardware and compiler techniques reduce their effect on pipeline throughput.
keywords_synonyms: Instruction pipeline; dependencies; Pipeline parallelism; dependency management; throughput; Computer Architecture
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Caches and virtual memory
definition: Memory-hierarchy mechanisms that exploit locality: caches retain frequently used data near processors, while virtual memory maps virtual addresses to physical storage.
scope: Cache levels, locality, mapping, replacement, write policies, TLBs and page translation.
core_principles: Locality; hierarchy; address translation; latency reduction.
semantic_description: Caches reduce average memory-access latency by exploiting temporal and spatial locality. Virtual memory provides address-space abstraction and protection; TLBs accelerate address translation.
keywords_synonyms: Memory hierarchy; paging; locality
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: I/O organization and interfaces
definition: Processor and system mechanisms used to communicate with peripheral devices and external interfaces.
scope: Programmed I/O, interrupts, DMA, buses, device controllers and interface protocols.
core_principles: Data transfer; synchronization; buffering; device abstraction.
semantic_description: I/O organization manages transfers between processors, memory and peripherals using mechanisms such as interrupts and DMA, balancing throughput, latency and processor involvement.
keywords_synonyms: I/O devices; interrupts; DMA
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Merge sort
definition: A stable comparison-based sorting algorithm that recursively divides a sequence and merges sorted sub-sequences.
scope: Divide-and-conquer decomposition, merge operation, stability and auxiliary storage.
core_principles: Divide and conquer; ordering; stability; predictable complexity.
semantic_description: Merge sort has O(n log n) time in the standard comparison model and typically uses O(n) auxiliary storage for array implementations.
keywords_synonyms: Divide and conquer; sorting; ordering; stability; predictable complexity; Design and Analysis of Algorithms
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Knapsack
definition: A family of optimization problems that selects items under a capacity constraint to maximize total value.
scope: For 0/1 knapsack, each item is selected at most once; state formulation, recurrence, dynamic programming and capacity/value constraints.
core_principles: Combinatorial optimization; optimal substructure; resource allocation; capacity constraints.
semantic_description: The 0/1 knapsack problem models discrete selection under a capacity constraint and admits pseudo-polynomial dynamic programming based on capacity. Fractional knapsack is a distinct variant with a greedy optimal solution.
keywords_synonyms: Dynamic programming; optimization; Combinatorial optimization; optimal substructure; resource allocation; capacity constraints
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Activity selection
definition: A scheduling problem that selects a maximum-size subset of mutually compatible activities given start and finish times.
scope: Compatibility, earliest-finish-time greedy rule, selection sequence and proof of optimality.
core_principles: Greedy choice; feasibility; optimal substructure.
semantic_description: The standard activity-selection problem is solved optimally by repeatedly selecting the compatible activity with the earliest finish time.
keywords_synonyms: Greedy algorithms; scheduling; Greedy choice; feasibility; optimal substructure; Design and Analysis of Algorithms
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Network flow
definition: A graph-based optimization model in which flow is sent through directed edges subject to capacity constraints from a source toward a sink.
scope: Flow conservation, capacities, residual networks, augmenting paths, max-flow/min-cut and common algorithms.
core_principles: Conservation; capacity constraints; residual improvement; optimality.
semantic_description: Maximum-flow algorithms repeatedly improve a feasible flow using residual capacity. The max-flow/min-cut theorem links maximum flow value to a minimum source-sink cut capacity.
keywords_synonyms: Graphs; optimization; residual networks
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: NP-complete problems
definition: Decision problems that are both in NP and NP-hard, meaning every problem in NP can be polynomial-time reduced to them.
scope: Polynomial verification, polynomial-time reductions, NP-hardness and representative problems.
core_principles: Computational complexity; reduction; tractability boundaries.
semantic_description: NP-completeness characterizes decision problems believed not to have polynomial-time algorithms unless P=NP. Proofs typically establish membership in NP and NP-hardness by reduction.
keywords_synonyms: Complexity classes; reductions; Computational complexity; reduction; tractability boundaries; Design and Analysis of Algorithms
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Process models
definition: Structured approaches for organizing software development activities, deliverables and control points across a development lifecycle.
scope: Waterfall, iterative/incremental, spiral, agile and hybrid lifecycle approaches; activities, feedback and change management.
core_principles: Lifecycle management; iteration; risk; stakeholder feedback.
semantic_description: Software process models organize requirements, design, implementation, verification and evolution. Their suitability depends on uncertainty, risk, constraints and stakeholder needs.
keywords_synonyms: Software lifecycle; development processes; Lifecycle management; iteration; risk; stakeholder feedback
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Continuous integration and delivery
definition: Software engineering practices that automate frequent integration, verification and delivery of software changes through a controlled pipeline.
scope: Build automation, version control integration, automated tests, artifact management, deployment automation and release controls.
core_principles: Automation; repeatability; feedback; quality assurance; traceability.
semantic_description: Continuous integration detects integration problems through frequent automated builds and tests. Continuous delivery keeps software in a releasable state through automated and controlled delivery practices.
keywords_synonyms: Version control; automated testing; deployment pipelines
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Use cases and requirements specification
definition: Techniques for eliciting, documenting and validating required system behaviour, qualities and constraints from stakeholder needs.
scope: Functional/non-functional requirements, actors, use cases, scenarios, acceptance criteria, traceability and validation.
core_principles: Stakeholder needs; completeness; consistency; verifiability; traceability.
semantic_description: Requirements engineering translates stakeholder needs into specifications that can be analyzed, validated and traced. Use cases primarily describe interactions and externally observable behaviour.
keywords_synonyms: Requirements engineering; use cases; Stakeholder needs; completeness; consistency; verifiability
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Design patterns
definition: Reusable, named design solutions to recurring software design problems within a stated context and set of trade-offs.
scope: Creational, structural and behavioural patterns; participants, collaborations, consequences and applicability.
core_principles: Abstraction; coupling/cohesion; reuse; trade-offs.
semantic_description: Design patterns document recurring design structures rather than finished code. Their value depends on context, appropriate abstraction and explicit trade-offs.
keywords_synonyms: Object-oriented design; software architecture; Abstraction; coupling/cohesion; reuse; trade-offs
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Unit and integration testing
definition: Testing practices that verify individual software units and their interactions with collaborating components.
scope: Test cases, fixtures, mocks/stubs, unit boundaries, integration strategies, interfaces and defect isolation.
core_principles: Verification; isolation; interface correctness; regression detection.
semantic_description: Unit tests focus on small software components, while integration tests examine interactions across component boundaries. Both support regression detection and defect localization.
keywords_synonyms: Software testing; verification; isolation; interface correctness; regression detection; Software Engineering
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Transmission media and signalling
definition: Physical means and signalling methods used to carry information across a communication channel.
scope: Copper, fibre and wireless media; bandwidth, attenuation, noise, modulation/encoding and transmission characteristics.
core_principles: Signal integrity; bandwidth; attenuation; interference.
semantic_description: Transmission media determine physical propagation characteristics, while signalling maps information to physical signals. Channel properties constrain achievable data rates and reliability.
keywords_synonyms: Physical layer; communication channels; Signal integrity; bandwidth; attenuation; interference
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Framing and MAC
definition: Data-link mechanisms that delimit frames and control access to a shared or point-to-point communication medium.
scope: Frame structure, error detection, MAC addressing, Ethernet, collision handling and medium-access methods.
core_principles: Framing; addressing; error detection; medium access.
semantic_description: Framing packages network-layer data for link transmission, while MAC mechanisms govern how stations access a shared medium and identify link-layer endpoints.
keywords_synonyms: Data link layer; Ethernet; Framing; addressing; error detection; medium access
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: IP addressing and routing
definition: Network-layer mechanisms for identifying interfaces or endpoints and selecting paths for forwarding packets between networks.
scope: IPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnetting, forwarding tables, routing principles and route selection.
core_principles: Hierarchical addressing; forwarding; reachability; path selection.
semantic_description: IP addressing identifies network-layer interfaces using address structures, while routing determines next-hop paths across interconnected networks.
keywords_synonyms: IP; subnetting; routing
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Transmission Control Protocol / User Datagram Protocol (TCP/UDP)
definition: Transport-layer protocols represented by TCP, a connection-oriented reliable byte-stream protocol, and UDP, a connectionless datagram transport.
scope: Ports, multiplexing, TCP sequencing/acknowledgement/congestion control and UDP datagrams.
core_principles: End-to-end transport; multiplexing; reliability; congestion management.
semantic_description: TCP provides ordered reliable byte-stream delivery with flow and congestion control. UDP provides minimal datagram transport without TCP's reliability, ordering or congestion-control semantics.
keywords_synonyms: Transport layer; sockets; End-to-end transport; multiplexing; reliability; congestion management
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)
definition: An application-layer request/response protocol used for transferring web resources and related representations.
scope: Methods, status codes, headers, message semantics, caching, persistent connections and HTTP over secure transports.
core_principles: Request/response; resource identification; stateless application semantics; extensibility.
semantic_description: HTTP defines application-level semantics for exchanging requests and responses. Web security and confidentiality are normally provided by using HTTP over TLS.
keywords_synonyms: Application layer; web protocols; Request/response; resource identification; stateless application semantics; extensibility
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Hooke's Law
definition: Within the linear elastic range of a material, stress is proportional to strain for the relevant loading mode.
scope: Normal stress/strain relation, elastic modulus, proportional limit and applicability to linear elasticity.
core_principles: Elasticity; proportionality; material stiffness.
semantic_description: Hooke's law provides the constitutive relation for linear elastic response, such as σ=Eε in uniaxial loading under the applicable assumptions.
keywords_synonyms: Stress-strain relation; elastic modulus; Elasticity; proportionality; material stiffness; Mechanics of Materials
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Flexure formula
definition: The beam flexure relation that connects bending stress to bending moment, cross-sectional geometry and distance from the neutral axis under stated beam assumptions.
scope: σ = My/I, neutral axis, second moment of area, bending moment and elastic-beam assumptions.
core_principles: Equilibrium; compatibility; elastic bending; section geometry.
semantic_description: The flexure formula is derived for slender beams under linear-elastic, small-deflection conditions where plane sections remain approximately plane.
keywords_synonyms: Bending moment; second moment of area; Equilibrium; compatibility; elastic bending; section geometry
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Bending stress distribution
definition: The spatial variation of normal bending stress across a beam cross-section caused by an applied bending moment.
scope: Linear stress distribution in elastic homogeneous sections, neutral axis, extreme fibres and section modulus.
core_principles: Stress distribution; neutral axis; section geometry.
semantic_description: For elastic bending of a homogeneous beam under the standard assumptions, bending stress varies linearly with distance from the neutral axis and reaches maximum magnitude at the extreme fibres.
keywords_synonyms: Flexure formula; section modulus; Stress distribution; neutral axis; section geometry; Mechanics of Materials
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Circular shafts
definition: Cylindrical structural members designed to transmit torque and resist associated torsional stresses and deformation.
scope: Solid/hollow shafts, torque, polar moment of inertia, torsional shear stress, angle of twist and power transmission.
core_principles: Torsion; shear stress; stiffness; strength.
semantic_description: Circular-shaft torsion relates applied torque to shear stress and twist using the polar second moment of area under the assumptions of elastic Saint-Venant torsion.
keywords_synonyms: Torsion; polar moment; shear stress; stiffness; strength; Mechanics of Materials
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Beam deflection methods
definition: Analytical methods used to determine displacement and slope of beams under transverse loading.
scope: Double integration, singularity functions, moment-area, conjugate beam and related elastic methods.
core_principles: Compatibility; stiffness; deformation; boundary conditions.
semantic_description: Beam deflection methods determine slope and displacement from load, bending stiffness and boundary conditions under linear-elastic beam assumptions.
keywords_synonyms: Flexure; moment-area theorem; Compatibility; stiffness; deformation; boundary conditions
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Viscosity
concept_category: Fluid Mechanics; Hydraulics and Hydraulic Engineering; Fluid Flow and Heat Transfer
definition: A measure of a fluid’s resistance to deformation and flow, arising from internal friction and relating shear stress to velocity gradient under Newtonian conditions.
scope: Concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
core_principles: Defining mechanism/properties; governing conditions; assumptions and limitations; application/performance criteria for Viscosity.
semantic_description: Dynamic viscosity relates shear stress to velocity gradient for a Newtonian fluid. Kinematic viscosity is dynamic viscosity divided by density.
keywords_synonyms: Newtonian fluids; shear stress; Defining mechanism/properties; governing conditions; assumptions and limitations; application/performance criteria for Viscosity
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Buoyancy
definition: The net upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed or floating body due to the pressure distribution in the fluid.
scope: Archimedes' principle, displaced-fluid volume, centre of buoyancy and floating equilibrium.
core_principles: Hydrostatic pressure; displaced volume; force equilibrium.
semantic_description: Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid for a body in a static fluid. Floating equilibrium depends on the relative locations of weight and buoyancy.
keywords_synonyms: Hydrostatics; pressure forces; Hydrostatic pressure; displaced volume; force equilibrium; Fluid Mechanics
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Continuity
definition: The mass-conservation relation requiring that mass entering, leaving and accumulating within a fluid system satisfy conservation of mass.
scope: Control-volume continuity, steady/unsteady flow, incompressible simplification and area-velocity relationships.
core_principles: Mass conservation; flux balance; continuity.
semantic_description: For steady incompressible one-dimensional flow, volumetric flow rate is conserved along a streamtube in the absence of sources or sinks, giving A₁V₁=A₂V₂.
keywords_synonyms: Mass conservation; control volumes; flux balance; continuity; Fluid Mechanics
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Reynolds number
definition: A dimensionless ratio comparing inertial effects with viscous effects in fluid flow.
scope: Re = ρVL/μ, characteristic length/velocity choices, similarity and flow-regime interpretation.
core_principles: Dimensional analysis; inertial-viscous balance; dynamic similarity.
semantic_description: Reynolds number helps characterize flow regimes and dynamic similarity. Critical values depend on geometry, disturbance level and flow configuration rather than being universal.
keywords_synonyms: Dimensional analysis; viscosity; inertial-viscous balance; dynamic similarity; Fluid Mechanics
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Head loss and pipe-flow analysis
definition: Analysis of pressure or energy losses associated with fluid flow through pipes and fittings.
scope: Darcy-Weisbach equation, friction factor, minor losses, hydraulic grade/energy lines and flow regimes.
core_principles: Energy conservation; friction; hydraulic resistance; efficiency.
semantic_description: Pipe-flow analysis quantifies major and minor head losses and their effect on required pressure head or pumping power.
keywords_synonyms: Reynolds number; viscosity; energy equation
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Truss and beam analysis
definition: Structural analysis procedures for determining internal forces and reactions in idealized trusses and beams under applied loads.
scope: Equilibrium, free-body diagrams, axial truss forces, shear and bending moment in beams.
core_principles: Equilibrium; load path; internal force; structural determinacy.
semantic_description: Truss and beam analysis converts external loading and supports into internal force resultants using equilibrium and stated idealizations.
keywords_synonyms: Statics; structural equilibrium; Equilibrium; load path; internal force; structural determinacy
:LABEL: KnowledgeConcept

name: Moment-area theorem
definition: Beam-deflection relations that connect changes in slope and deflection to areas and first moments of the M/EI diagram.
scope: Theorem 1 for slope change, theorem 2 for tangential deviation, boundary conditions and sign conventions.
core_principles: Curvature; integration; compatibility.
semantic_description: The moment-area method integrates beam curvature through geometric properties of the bending-moment diagram to obtain slope and deflection.
